brief: 6 typefaces with stories so good you'll use them on purpose for the rest of your life.

slots.description: A wonky, soft-serve-inspired variable serif from Undercase Type. Its playful axes and retro personality make it perfect for bold headlines with vintage charm.
Claus Eggers Sørensen’s high-contrast transitional serif draws from Scotch Roman and Baskerville, bringing editorial elegance to digital screens.
Florian Karsten evolved Space Mono into this proportional grotesk, channeling brutalist geometry and utilitarian clarity for modern interfaces.
Built from 19th-century wood type, this eclectic sans collages historical cuts into one quirky, confident voice for cultural brands.
Commissioned for a European blockchain initiative, this futuristic display face merges tech aesthetics with open-source accessibility and geometric flair.
Designed by Instrument, this refined editorial serif pairs razor-sharp precision with warm, contemporary grace for luxury layouts.
Michael Sharanda’s geometric sans bridges humanist warmth and neutral utility, becoming a go-to workhorse for product design worldwide.

slots.body: These six typefaces prove that great design starts with character. Save this guide and reference it for your next project.
